# 7-Zip parity

<!-- Generated by scripts/parity.py render from tests/data/parity. Do not edit. -->

This page lists everything 7-Zip 26.05 extracts and how Zipper handles it. The [roadmap](../roadmap/m10-parity-matrix.md) moves every row to native, or records why it is dropped.

Each row has one status.

- `native` means Zipper reads it in process.
- `partial` means Zipper reads some of it in process, as the note says.
- `missing` means Zipper does not do it. No row goes to 7-Zip, since Zipper never runs 7-Zip.
- `dropped` means Zipper leaves it out on purpose, as the note says.
- `refused` means Zipper refuses it for licence reasons, as the note says.

A proof is a corpus archive or a test. `tests/parity.rs` extracts every corpus archive. A native row must match the tree 7-Zip extracted when the corpus was built. A missing row must be refused with nothing published. A refused row, and a refused archive of another row, must be refused with an error that says Zipper does not read it, with nothing published.

| Status | Rows |
| --- | ---: |
| `native` | 87 |
| `partial` | 1 |
| `missing` | 4 |
| `dropped` | 2 |
| `refused` | 18 |

5 rows have no proof yet. The milestone that moves a row adds a corpus archive for it, or a test when the row is a switch.
